# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 94 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 94 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_094_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 11

**1** "First learn who I am," he said to me. "Lord, instruct me," I replied. "Who do you suppose the tall man is — the one who bears the name of the Son of God?" **2** I replied, "The Son of God is the one clothed in the Holy Spirit of God." "You have spoken rightly," he said; "for the Son of God is the one clothed in the Holy Spirit, **3** and through him the whole world was created and is sustained. And note this: he is more ancient than all creation, and through him God laid the foundations of all things. He himself is the foundation and the cornerstone." **4** "But why," I asked, "does he sometimes appear as aged and sometimes as young?" "Because the Son of God is pre-existent," he answered, "and appeared to his servants at both the beginning and the end; he appeared as ancient to those of the former covenant, and as young and new to those of the new covenant. **5** For what you see is the new age — he renews all things and makes them new. **6** The old things have been accomplished and have passed away. And he appointed twelve people and gave them authority to walk in his commandments; after these he appointed twelve more, and then seven. All of these walked in the power of the Son of God."

---

### Translator's Note
This is the Shepherd's most concentrated christological statement. The Son of God as: (1) clothed in the Holy Spirit, (2) pre-existent creator, (3) foundation and cornerstone, (4) renewer of all things — and his appearing as old (to the old covenant community) and young (to the new). The three tiers of leadership — 12, 12, 7 — likely refer to apostles, teachers, and deacons. SOPHIA follows LOGOS; PNEUMA's "new creation" gloss in v. 5 is theologically apt but expands the Greek.
